dataPalettes.meaning: Tracked-sample share counts distinct individuals in the selected period. Observation heat counts unique records against the selected species’ full-period sample before filtering months; neither estimates abundance.

accessibility.focus: 2px pale outline with 5–6px offset; native select has focus-within wrapper.
accessibility.reducedMotion: Home starts on a still poster; no stamp tilt, density/observation crossfade or atlas-panel, atlas-bird or collection arrival animation. LivingBirdFilm requires manual Play, including post-action flight, with an 80ms video reveal. Night ambient fade shortens to 80ms.
accessibility.touch: No pointer tilt; touch hint replaces movement hint.
accessibility.journey: Native checkbox actions and separate after-dark confirmation; focus moves to the new Lights Out stage heading. Mobile navigation closes on Escape and returns focus to its trigger.
accessibility.film: Muted inline playback, persistent Play/Pause, still fallback and failure copy. Hidden or offscreen films pause. The post-action native dialog focuses Skip, supports Escape and leaves the already-recorded night intact.
accessibility.atlas: A shared native species select with previous/next buttons and a native 1–12 month range work in both scopes. Place search is non-modal; Escape closes it and restores trigger focus. Geolocation is requested only by activating Near home.

scope.legacy: Six original quiz pages are archived, unrouted, under web/legacy/species/. Previously completed quiz marks remain recognized.

journeys.mapContext: One month/layer URL model supports both scopes and validated local returnTo links through profiles, gallery and Lights Out. Legacy nearbyMonth/nearbyLayer are normalized. A location-less view=nearby link opens place search without requesting geolocation.
journeys.nearby: Near home explicitly requests approximate geolocation and moves the existing map. Find a place / Change place opens a non-modal city search panel. The shared bird chooser, month range and opacity filter the loaded 25km sample without refitting or requerying. Back to migration restores the preceding historical bird and retains month.
journeys.collection: Seven illustrated stamps, four cosmetic finishes, All / Saved filters and device-local bookmarks; ten bird profiles with photographic hero footage and a separate keepsake section.
journeys.lightsOut: Understand, Take action, Remember. City-bird film accompanies action selection. After confirming an action was completed after dark, record one entry per local date immediately, then offer eight seconds of archival flight. Pause, Skip, Escape and replay are available; reduced motion starts on the poster. Darkened completion and journal support undo/removal.

observationHeat.denominator: Selected species’ unique valid records across the full source period, unchanged by month filters.
observationHeat.rendering: Finite local kernel with latitude-corrected longitudinal support, screen compositing and pearl isobands. No minimum pixel radius on zoom-out. Switch to original points for record provenance.

films.identity: Exact species is not established by original filenames. Shared or unverified archival footage is labelled independently from profile/data identity.
films.profileLayout: Desktop directional reading mask leaves the subject visible; mobile uses a separate 390px film strip after the introduction. Stamps follow below.

mapControls.bird: One native species selector, previous/next controls, available stamp, save/profile/collection links. Nearby options come from the chosen area’s source records.
mapControls.month: One native January–December range with twelve labels, All months and play/pause, shared on desktop/mobile and between scopes.
mapControls.location: Place selection changes the existing map centre and observation sample. Nearby species, month and opacity retain viewport and loaded sample.
mapControls.permission: Near home calls geolocation only after explicit activation; place search and remembered-area selection do not request it.

narrative.overview:
BirdRadar places oversized, closely set sans-serif type and quiet controls directly over wildlife film, dark landscape imagery and satellite geography. Soft directional masks create reading space; open composition and tonal contrast do most of the grouping. Rich colour belongs to measured geographic fields and illustrated postage stamps.

The stamps provide the tactile counterpart: intact bird artwork, visible paper perforations and separate optical finishes. One continuous map presents historical tracks and nearby observations, deriving each field’s shape and coverage from source records. Bird profiles connect those records to keepsakes; Lights Out turns that interest into a chosen action at home, followed by a quieter, darker landscape.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed imagery and geography with dissolving dark masks.
Large Geom headings; compact, unboxed navigation and controls.
Milky species density fields and transparent, perforated foil stamps.
Visible data context and sources, device-local keepsakes and night journals, and reduced-motion alternatives.

rules.name: The Evidence Colour Rule
rules.body: Both fields use fixed 0%, 5%, 10%+ colour. Tracking counts distinct individuals in the selected period; observation heat uses the selected species’ full-period record count even when months change. Neither estimates abundance, and observations do not establish routes.

rules.name: The Material Boundary Rule
rules.body: Keep foil and diffraction inside the stamp's alpha mask. Navigation and ordinary controls remain quiet and matte.

dos: Do preserve the locally bundled Geom face, oversized headings and generous open space.
Do keep terrain, geographic labels, legends and attribution legible beneath and around the density field.
Do derive visible coverage, dates and sample counts from the selected real records.
Do preserve transparent stamp edges and keep bird identity and printed artwork readable through each finish.
Do retain visible focus, native keyboard controls, pause controls and reduced-motion behavior.
Do keep map context intact across the bird, collection and night-action journey.
Do make location requests explicit and separate saved keepsakes from self-reported night actions.
Do keep living footage visible, its identity limits legible, and flight playback optional after recording.
Do preserve the same map, bird chooser and month control when moving between historical journeys and nearby observations.
donts: Don't replace the cinematic world with boxed dashboard panels or pervasive hard dividers.
Don't turn UI headings into serif type; fine print embedded in stamp artwork is a separate material.
Don't label historical samples live, join independent observations into routes, or read brightness as abundance.
Don't invent routes or flowing particles to match a mockup, or crossfade data across a changed geographic frame.
Don't present a cosmetic finish or saved bookmark as a quiz award, account sync or permanent ownership.
Don't interpret a Lights Out journal entry as sensor evidence, a bird-presence forecast or a measured conservation outcome.
